title: Larkholm ferry renewal
question: How might fictional stakeholders on Larkholm respond to replacing the island ferry with a battery-electric vessel?

participants.name: Larkholm Island Council

quote.text: The national Clean Coasts Fund would pay 40% of the electric vessel's cost if the Council commits before 30 September.

participants.rationale: The Council chooses between the refit and the electric vessel.

participants.name: Finance Committee

quote.text: The Finance Committee will not raise the annual ferry subsidy above $1.8 million.

participants.rationale: Sets the subsidy ceiling the plan has to fit under.

participants.name: Harbour-ward councillors

quote.text: Councillors from the harbour ward have said they will not back a plan that cuts winter service for islanders.

participants.rationale: Say they would not back a plan that cuts winter service.

participants.name: Larkholm Ferry Company

quote.text: The operator has proposed a fare increase to cover part of that cost; the Council has not taken a position on the size of any increase.

participants.rationale: Runs the route and proposes the timetable and fare changes.

participants.name: Islander households

quote.text: The Association surveyed 1,150 islander households and received replies from 52% of them.

participants.rationale: Depend on the ferry and bear the timetable and fare changes.

participants.name: Larkholm Residents' Association

quote.text: The Association asks the Council to guarantee at least six winter sailings a day and to cap any fare increase at 5%.

participants.rationale: Speaks for islanders and sets two conditions.

participants.name: Larkholm Health Centre

quote.text: The Larkholm Health Centre reports about 140 patient trips a month to mainland clinics between November and March, including dialysis appointments that cannot be rescheduled.

participants.rationale: Its patients depend on winter sailings.

participants.name: Winter commuters

quote.text: Many nurses, teachers and shift workers commute by the first and last sailings of the day.

participants.rationale: Rely on the first and last sailings.

quote.text: The Alliance polled 400 visitors and residents and found that 74% support an electric ferry.

participants.name: Harbour Business Council

quote.text: The Business Council supports an electric ferry because it would strengthen the island's green image.

participants.rationale: Island businesses that gain from summer visitors.

quote.text: Visitors account for about 70% of summer crossings, and summer visitor spending is worth around $9.5 million a year to island shops, guest houses and cafes.

participants.name: Clean Coasts Fund

quote.text: The national Clean Coasts Fund would pay 40% of the electric vessel's cost if the Council commits before 30 September.

participants.rationale: Would pay 40% of the electric vessel if the Council commits in time.

participants.name: Terminal grid operator

quote.text: Grid upgrades for charging at both terminals are expected to take 14 to 18 months, and the diesel vessel would keep running throughout.

participants.rationale: Somebody has to do the grid upgrades; the text names no operator.

participants.name: Ferry crew
participants.rationale: A reduced winter timetable and a new vessel change their work; no source speaks for them.

participants.name: Passengers with limited mobility
participants.rationale: Depend on boarding and timetable arrangements; nobody speaks for them.

participants.name: Freight and delivery carriers
participants.rationale: The island's supplies cross by ferry; the sources do not mention goods.

constraints.quote: The Finance Committee will not raise the annual ferry subsidy above $1.8 million.
constraints.rationale: A stated ceiling on the subsidy.
The grant is lost if the Council does not commit before it.

constraints.quote: Any decision to buy a new vessel needs evidence of sustained use and a funding plan before the March budget vote.
constraints.rationale: A procedural condition for buying a vessel.

constraints.quote: Charging at both terminals needs grid upgrades that will take 14 to 18 months, so the diesel vessel must keep sailing until they are finished.
constraints.rationale: A physical lead time that fixes the order of work.

constraints.quote: Councillors from the harbour ward have said they will not back a plan that cuts winter service for islanders.
constraints.rationale: A stated political position, not a rule.

constraints.quote: Battery vessels have less power in reserve in heavy weather, so more winter sailings may be cancelled in storms.
Its maintenance bill has risen every year since 2021, and the operating contract with the Larkholm Ferry Company ends in 2028.
constraints.rationale: A contract end date fixes when arrangements must change.

constraints.quote: The Larkholm Health Centre reports about 140 patient trips a month to mainland clinics between November and March, including dialysis appointments that cannot be rescheduled.
constraints.rationale: Medical trips cannot be moved, so winter service has a floor.

constraints.quote: The Association asks the Council to guarantee at least six winter sailings a day and to cap any fare increase at 5%.
constraints.rationale: A request with two numbers; not binding.

gap.removeText: Its maintenance bill has risen every year since 2021, and the operating contract with the Larkholm Ferry Company ends in 2028.
gap.rationale: The only statement of the operating contract is removed.
